title: Sell Mineral Rights in Malaga, NM
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Malaga, NM
metaDescription: Malaga sits right on the Texas line in the core Delaware Basin, among the most heavily drilled ground in Eddy County. We buy mineral and royalty interests here direct.
heroLead: Malaga sits close enough to the Texas line that you could throw a rock into Loving County, and the drilling around it looks exactly like what you'd expect from that address.
intro: This little community along the Pecos River sits over some of the densest horizontal Wolfcamp and Bone Spring development anywhere in Eddy County. If your family's minerals are near Malaga, there's a good chance more than one operator has run laterals across the acreage in the last several years.

sections.heading: Core basin, high well density
paragraphs: Malaga sits deep enough in the Delaware Basin that the shelf geology you see farther north around Artesia doesn't apply. Multiple Wolfcamp benches and Bone Spring sands stack up thick here, and operators have run repeated multi-well pads across the area for years, which is exactly why activity-driven offers on Malaga acreage tend to run strong.

sections.heading: Checking every unit instead of one well
paragraphs: Given the pad density around Malaga, it's common for a single tract to be pooled into more than one spacing unit across different intervals. We check every unit your acreage could be part of before quoting, since pricing off just one well here regularly undersells what an owner actually has.

sections.heading: What makes Malaga different from shelf-side Lea County
paragraphs: Owners who've heard offer numbers from friends or relatives up on the Northwest Shelf sometimes expect a similar range down here, and that's usually not a fair comparison. Malaga sits in genuinely different, thicker pay with more active recent development, and we'll walk through exactly why the numbers can differ so much between the two areas.

faqs.question: Why is drilling so dense around Malaga?
faqs.answer: It sits in the core Delaware Basin with thick, stacked Wolfcamp and Bone Spring pay close to the Texas line, similar to the geology across the border in Loving and Reeves counties. Operators have run repeated multi-well programs here for years.

faqs.question: Could my tract be part of more than one spacing unit?
faqs.answer: Yes, that's common around Malaga given how many wells have been drilled across different intervals. We check every unit tied to your acreage rather than pricing off a single well.

faqs.question: How fast does a Malaga interest typically close?
faqs.answer: With clean title and a current division order, most close within three to four weeks. We'll confirm your specific timeline once we've reviewed your records.

faqs.question: Why would Malaga acreage be worth more than shelf-side Lea County acreage?
faqs.answer: Malaga sits in the core Delaware Basin with thicker, stacked pay and denser recent horizontal development than most Northwest Shelf acreage farther north. We price each tract on its own record, but the underlying geology and activity level genuinely differ.
